Take the matter of dress, and we have 1 Pet. 3:3- 4 “ Do not let your adorning be external — the braiding of hair and the putting on of gold jewelry, or the clothing you wear — but let your adorning be the hidden person of the heart with the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which in God’s sight is very precious .” and 1 Tim. 2:9 - 10 “ likewise also that women should adorn themselves in respectable apparel, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or costly attire, but with what is proper for women who profess godliness —with good works.” Take the matter of conversation, and we have Eph. 4:29 “ Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up, as fits the occasion, that it may give grace to those who hear . ” , and 5:4 “ Let there be no filthiness nor foolish talk nor crude joking, which are out of place, but instead let there be thanksgiving .” Take the matter of avenging injuries and standing up for your rights, and we have (Romans.12:19- 21) “ Beloved, never avenge yourselves, but leave it to the wrath of God, for it is written, “Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord.” To the contrary, “if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink; for by so doing you will hear burning coals on his head.” Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good ,” and (Matthew. 5:38 - 48) “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I say to you, do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also. And if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well. And if anyone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles. Give to the one who begs from you, and do not refuse the one who would borrow from you. You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You therefore must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.” “ For this is a gracious thing, when, mindful of God, one endures sorrows while suffering unjustly. For what credit is it if, when you sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if when you do good and suffer for it you endure, this is a gracious thing in the sight of God. For to this you have been called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in his steps .”(1Peter. 2:19-21) Take the matter of forgiving one another, and we have (Ephesians.4:32) “ Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you.” Mark 11:25- 26 “And whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father also who is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses .” Take the matter of conformity to the world, and we have (Romans 12:20) “ Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect. ” and (1 John 2:15- 17) “ Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world — the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes and pride of life — is not from the Father but is from the world. And the world is passing away along with its desires, but whoever does the will of God abides forever. “ You adulterous people! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Therefore, whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.”(James 4:4) Take the matter of anxieties of all kinds, and we have (Matthew 6:25- 34) “Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will put on. Isn't life more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they? And which of you, by being anxious, can add a single hour to his span of life? And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today is alive and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith? Therefore, do not be anxious, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’ For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. “Therefore , do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble. “ Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.”( Philippians 4:6-7) I only give these as examples to show how very full and practical the Bible guidance is. If you are confused, first, check if the Bible addresses your question. Ask God to reveal His will to you through the Scriptures. And whatever shall seem to you to be plainly taught there, that you must obey. Reading and meditating on this record of God's mind and will enlightens us. The inspiring Spirit will do so. Our obedience will then be, as if, a present, living word. It will be as if our Lord spoke it to us today from Heaven. The Bible is an ancient message from God, sent to us long ago. It is also a present message, sent to us now each time we read it. "My words are spirit and life. You must obey them. It's a command, personal and present." But we must remember, the Bible is a book of principles. It is not a group of unrelated sayings . Isolated texts may be used to sanction things. These are opposed by Scripture's principles. I recently heard of a Christian woman at a Western meeting. The text, "For we walk by faith, and not by sight," brought it to mind. She felt it was a command to be literally obeyed. So, she blindfolded herself and insisted on walking up and down the aisle to illustrate the walk of faith. She soon stumbled and fell against the stove, burning herself. Then, she wondered at the mysterious dispensation. Applying Scripture and her common sense would have saved her from the delusion. The second test, therefore, is our own higher judgment, or common sense. It is as true now as in Solomon's time. A "man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels." His exhortation still binds us: "Get wisdom, the principal thing. “Wi th all you're getting, get understanding." The Scriptures say it is vital for God's children to use all their abilities on their journey through this world. They are to use their outward faculties for their outward walk, and their inward faculties for their inward walk. They might as well expect to be "kept" from stubbing their toes if they walk blindfolded. It's the same as expecting to be "kept" from spiritual stumbling if they ignore their judgment and common sense. I asked a "sound mind" Christian how she told false spirits from the Holy Spirit. She replied, "I rap them over the head and see if they have any common sense." Some may say, "But we should not depend on our human understanding in divine things." I answer that we should not depend on our unenlightened understanding. We should rely on our judgment and common sense, which the Spirit of God has enlightened. That is, God will speak to us through the faculties He has Himself given us, and not independently of them. We must use our eyes when we walk, no matter how faithful we are. Similarly, we must use our minds in our inner lives. The third and last test is that of providential circumstances. If a “leading” is of God, a way will always open for it. Our Lord assures us of this in John 10:4. It says, “When he has brought out all his own, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice. ” Notice here the expressions “goes before,” and “ follows .” He goes before to open a way, and we are to follow in the way thus opened. A Christian should not force his way and trample opposition. That is never a sign of a Divine leading. If the Lord “goes before” us, He will open all doors for us, and we shall not need ourselves to hammer them down. The fourth point is this: We must test our impressions by the other three voices. We must also test those voices by our inward impressions. If we feel a "stop in our minds" about anything, we must wait until it is removed before acting. A Christian, who had quickly advanced in the Divine life, gave me this secret: "I always mind the checks." We must not ignore our inner voice, nor ride roughshod over it, any more than we must the other three voices of which I have spoken. These four voices, then, will always be found to agree in any truly Divine leading. The voice of our impressions, the voice of Scripture, the voice of our own sanctified judgment. The voice of providential circumstances. If these four do not agree at first, we must wait until they do. A divine sense of “oughtness,” derived from the harmony of all God’s various voices, is the only safe foundation for any action. I have guarded the points of danger. So, please let me out. I long for the joy of this direct communication of God's will to us. It seems to me to be the grandest of privileges. In the first place, that God should love me enough to care about the details of my life is perfectly wonderful. And that He would tell me all about it. And, to know how to live and walk to perfectly please Him, seems almost too good to be true. We never care about the little details of people’s lives unless we love them. We don't care what most people do or how they spend their time. But when we love someone, we start to care. God's care for us proves His love. It's a great blessing that He speaks to us about everything in our lives. This includes our duties, pleasures, friendships, and all we do, think, or say. You must know this in your own experience, dear reader. Only then will you find the joy and privilege of a life hid with Christ in God. It is one of its most precious gifts. God promises to work in us to will and to do of His good pleasure. This means He will take control of our will and work it for us. His suggestions will come to us as desires, not commands. They will originate in our will; we shall feel as though we wanted to do so and so, not as though we must. This makes it a service of perfect liberty. For it is always easy to do what we desire, no matter how difficult the circumstances. Every mother knows she could get perfect obedience from her child. She just needs to control his will, making him want to do what she wants. And this is what our Father does for His children in the new dispensation. He writes His laws on our hearts and minds. We love them. Our affections and judgment, not our fears, draw us to obey. The Holy Spirit usually guides by impressing a desire to do or avoid certain things. In prayer, the soul feels a sudden suggestion about a duty. “I would like to do this or the other,” it thinks, “I wish I could.” Or the suggestion may come as a question, “I wonder whether I had not better do so and so?” Or it may be only at first in the way of a conviction that such is the right and best thing to be done. The matter should be committed to the Lord. We must instantly choose to obey Him. If the suggestion agrees with the Scriptures, a holy judgment, and the circumstances, we should obey it. Immediate obedience is the safest and easiest course. When the Spirit speaks, it is easy to obey. But if the soul hesitates and reasons, it becomes harder to obey. The first convictions are usually right in a fully surrendered heart. God is faithful and will make His voice heard above all others. Such convictions, therefore, should never be met by reasoning. Prayer and trust are the only safe attitudes of the soul. But even these should be brief. We must act before the time passes and we miss the blessing. If the suggestion is unclear and doubt arises, we should wait for further insight. This is especially true if our friends disagree. The Scripture rule is, “Whatsoever is not of faith is sin” which means plainly that we must never act in doubt. A clear conviction of right is the only safe guide. But we must wait in faith. We must fully surrender, saying, "Yes," to our Lord's will, whatever it may be. Our troubles stem from a lack of will. Next, many doubt any real Divine guidance. God's children are very skeptical here. They read the promises and feel the need. But, they cannot believe that someone will guide them. It's as if God wants us to obey His voice, but didn't know how to make us hear and understand Him. It is, thus, very possible for God to speak, but for the soul not to hear, because it does not believe He is speaking. No earthly parent or master could guide his children or servants if they did not believe him or accept his voice as his true will. God, who spoke to the fathers in many ways, still speaks. He wants to see if any souls will obey His will. Every moment of our lives our Father is seeking to reveal Himself to us. “ Jesus said to her, “I who speak to you am he.”(John 4:26) I that speak in your heart, in your circumstances, in your losses, in your gains, in your sorrows, and in your joys, am He. "I speak everywhere and in everything." So, we must have perfect faith that the Lord's voice is speaking to us. It will teach and lead us. He will give us wisdom for our guidance. After asking for guidance, we must follow our strongest sense of what we should do. A few rules can help us with this. I. We must believe that God will guide us. II. We must surrender our own will to His guidance. III. We must hearken for the Divine voice. IV. We must wait for the divine harmony. When we are certain of God’s guidance, we must follow it without hesitation. He is our t rue home. The path may be difficult and narrow, but nothing else can satisfy a heart that longs for Him. How little of that path you have walked, my soul! Take courage, and let the thought of God draw you further. The perfect way may be hard for the flesh, but it is not hard for love. If you were desperate for God, how quickly you would move toward Him. Do not give your duties to God reluctantly — let your hands be open and free. Fix your eyes on Jesus and consider how freely He gave His love to you. True perfection requires only a heart that remains at peace throughout the day, listening for the Spirit’s voice moment by moment. Keep your conscience sensitive — do not ignore His quiet nudges. And go wherever His grace leads you.

fields.title: Concerning Temptation
fields.body_html:
Temptation is not a sign of failure but a part of spiritual growth. It’s not a sin to be tempted, only to yield to it. Discouragement is a trap, and trusting God with temptation strengthens faith. Enduring temptation leads to spiritual growth and the "crown of life" promised to those who persevere.

Some very big mistakes are made about temptation in this life of faith. First, people expect that, after the soul rests in God, temptations will cease. They believe the promised salvation is from both temptation and being tempted. When they find the Canaanite still in the land, and see the great, walled cities, they are discouraged. They think they must have gone wrong and that this cannot be the true land after all.

Next, they mistakenly see temptation as sin. They blame themselves for it, but it's the enemy's fault.

This leads to condemnation and discouragement. If it continues, it ends in sin. The enemy makes an easy prey of a discouraged soul; so that we fall often from the very fear of having fallen. To solve the first difficulty, I must refer to Scripture. It says the Christian life is a constant warfare. It also says we must, especially when seated in heavenly places in Christ Jesus, wrestle against spiritual enemies there.

Their power and skill to tempt us must be far superior to any we've ever encountered.

Temptations usually grow tenfold in strength after we start the interior life, not decrease. Their power must not lead us to doubt that we have found the true, abiding place. Strong temptations are generally a sign of great grace, rather than of little grace. When the Israelites first left Egypt, the Lord did not lead them through the Philistines' land, the nearest route. God said, “When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near. For God said, “Lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.” But, when they learned to trust Him, He allowed their enemies to attack. In their wilderness journey, they met few enemies and fought few battles. In the land, they faced seven great nations and thirty-one kings. They had to conquer walled cities and defeat giants.

They could not have fought the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites until they had entered their land. Your temptations, dear Christian, may prove you are in the land you seek to enter. They are unique to that land. Never let your temptations make you doubt that you are in the promised "heavenly places."

The second mistake is not quite so easy to deal with. It's almost pointless to say that temptation is not sin. Yet, most distress comes from not understanding this. The very suggestion of wrong seems to bring pollution with it. The evil agency not recognized, the poor, tempted soul fears it must be very bad, and far from God, to have had such thoughts. It is as though a burglar broke into a man's house to steal.

When the owner began to resist him, the burglar accused him of being the thief. It is the enemy's clever trick to trap us.

He comes and whispers evil ideas to us: doubts, blasphemies, jealousy, envy, and pride. Then he says, "Oh, how wicked you must be to think of such things!" It is plain that you do not trust the Lord. If you did, these things would not have entered your heart. This reasoning seems true, so the soul accepts it.

It then feels condemned and discouraged. From there, it is easy to fall into sin. One of the most fatal things in the life of faith is discouragement.

One of the most helpful is cheerfulness. A wise man once said that, in overcoming temptations, cheerfulness was the key. It was the first, second, and third thing. We must expect to conquer. That is why the Lord often told Joshua, “Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go ” (Joshua 1:9). And it is also the reason He says to us, “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid” (John14:27) .

The power of temptation is in the fainting of our own hearts. The enemy knows this. He always tries to discourage us at the start of his assaults, if he can.

Sometimes, we feel discouraged. We think it's righteous grief and disgust at ourselves for being tempted. But it's really an embarrassment . We are ashamed because we secretly congratulated ourselves. We believed our tastes were too pure and our separation from the world too complete for such things to tempt us. We expected something from ourselves. We are disappointed to find it lacking.

As a result, we are discouraged. This embarrassment and discouragement are worse than the temptation. They seem humble, but they only stem from wounded self-love.

True humility can bear to see its own weakness and foolishness revealed. It never expected anything from itself. It knows its only hope must be in God. So, instead of discouraging the soul from trusting, it drives it to a deeper and more utter trust. But counterfeit humility, born of self, plunges the soul into despair. It drives it into the very sin it so despises. I remember once hearing an allegory that illustrated this to me wonderfully. Satan called together a council of his servants to consult how they might make a good man sin. One evil spirit started up and said, “I will make him sin.” “How will you do it?” asked Satan. “I will set before him the pleasures of sin,” was the reply; “I will tell him of its delights and the ri ch rewards it brings.” “Ah,” said Satan, “that will not do; he has tried, it, and knows better than that.”

Then another spirit started up and said, “I will make him sin.”

“What will you do?” asked Satan. “I will tell him of the pains and sorrows of v irtue. I will show him that virtue has no delights, and brings no rewards.” “Ah, no!” exclaimed Satan, “That will not do at all.

He has tried it. He knows, 'wisdom's ways are pleasant, and her paths are peace.' Another said, I will make him sin. And what will you do? Asked Satan, again. I will discourage his soul, was the short reply. Ah, that will do,” cried Satan, “that will do! We shall conquer him now.” And they did. An old writer says, all discouragement is from the devil. I wish every Christian would remember this and keep it as a pocket-piece. We must fly from discouragement as we would from sin. But this is impossible if we fail to recognize the true agency in temptation. For if the temptations are our own fault, we cannot help being discouraged. But they are not.

The Bible says, “Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him. ”(James 1:12) It urges us to "count it all joy when we fall into diverse temptations." Temptation, therefore, cannot be sin. It is no more a sin to hear evil whispers in our souls than to hear the swearing of bad men as we pass along the street. The sin only comes in either case by our stopping and joining in with them. If, when the wicked thoughts come, we turn from them at once, as we would from wicked talk, and ignore them, we do not sin. But if we carry them on in our minds, and roll them under our tongues, and dwell on them with a half consent of our will to them as true, then we sin.

We may be enticed by evil a thousand times a day without sin, and we cannot help these enticing. But if the enemy can make us think his temptations are our sin, he will have won half the battle. He will then likely win completely.

A dear lady once came to me under great darkness, simply from not understanding this. She had been very happy in her faith for some time. She had been free from temptation, and thought she would never be tempted again. But suddenly a very peculiar form of temptation had assailed her, which had horrified her. She found that the moment she began to pray, dreadful thoughts of all kinds would rush into her mind. She had lived a very sheltered, innocent life. These thoughts seemed so awful to her, that she felt she must be one of the wicked of sinners to have them. She began by thinking she could not have entered into the rest of faith. She ended by concluding that she had never been born again.

Her soul was in an agony of distress.

I told her that these dreadful thoughts were the enemy's doing. He came to her the moment she kneeled in prayer and filled her mind with them. She was not to blame for them at all. She could not help them any more than she could help hearing a wicked man blaspheme in her presence. I urged her to see them as from the enemy. She should not blame or discourage herself. Instead, she should turn to Jesus and commit them to Him. I showed her how much the enemy had gained. They made her think these thoughts were her own. This condemned and discouraged her. I assured her she would win quickly if she ignored them. She should turn her back on them and look to the Lord.

She grasped the truth, and the next time these thoughts came she said to the enemy, “I have found you out now. It is you who are suggesting these dreadful thoughts to me, and I hate them, and will have nothing to do with them. The Lord is my Saviour; take them to Him, and settle them in His presence.”

The baffled enemy, found out, fled in confusion. Her soul was perfectly delivered.

Another thing also. The enemy knows that if a Christian sees a hint of evil as his, he will reject it. He will do so more quickly than if it seems to be his own mind's suggestion. If Satan began each temptation with, "I am Satan, your enemy; I have come to make you sin," we would likely resist. He has to hide himself in order to make his baits attractive. Our victory will be easier if we are not ignorant of his tricks. We must recognize him at his first approach. We also make a mistake about temptations. We think that all time spent fighting them is wasted. Hours pass, and we seem to have made no progress, because we have been so beset with temptations. But, we may have served God more truly during these hours than in our freer times, when we faced fewer temptations.

Temptation is really more the devil’s wrath against God, than against us. He cannot touch our Saviour.

But, he can wound Him by conquering us. Our ruin matters to him only as it does this. So, we fight our Lord's battles when we resist temptation. In these cases, an hour is worth a day's time. We read, “Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him ."(James 1:12).I am sure this means to endure its continuance and frequent recurrence.

Nothing cultivates the grace of patience like enduring temptation. And, nothing drives the soul to depend on the Lord Jesus like it. And finally, nothing brings more glory to our Lord than the trial of our faith, which comes through many temptations. It is said to be more precious than gold, though tested by fire. We, who endure the trial, shall receive a reward. It is "the crown of life" which the Lord has promised to those who love Him.”

We cannot wonder at the Holy Ghost's urging at the start of the Book of James: " Count it all joy, my brothers, when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness. And let steadfastness have its full effect, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing. ”(James 1:2)Temptation is God's tool to complete our perfection. So, the enemy's own weapons are turned against him. We see that all things, even temptations, can work for good to them that love God.

To resist temptations, I don’t need to tell my audience: it is by faith. For this is, of course, the foundation upon which the whole interior life rests. Our one great motto is throughout, “We are nothing, and Christ is all.” A nd always and everywhere we have started to stand, and walk, and overcome, and live by faith. We have found our own helplessness. We cannot help ourselves. Our only way, therefore, is to hand the temptation over to our Lord and trust Him to conquer it for us.

But when we put it into His hands, we must leave it there. We must commit to Him for victory as we did for salvation. He must do all for us in the one case, as completely as in the other. It was faith only then, and it must be faith only now.

The Lord works miracles in conquering the temptations of those who trust Him. Thousands can testify to this. But I cannot expand on this now. I aimed to show temptation in its true light, not to detail the way to overcome it. I want to free good, faithful souls from bondage. They will be trapped if they confuse temptation with sin. They must understand temptation's true nature and use. I want them to know that temptations are vital for our souls' growth. Whatever their source, God uses them to build in us graces of character that would otherwise be missing.

Wherever temptation is, there is God also, superintending and controlling its power. “Where were you, Lord I, while I was being tempted?” cried the saint of the desert. "Close beside you, my son, all the while," was the tender reply. Temptations try us. We are worth nothing if we are not tried. They develop our spiritual strength and courage and knowledge, and our development is the one thing God cries for.

How shallow would all our spirituality be if it were not for temptations? "Blessed is the man who endures temptation. He will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love Him." This "crown of life" will be worth all the trials and endurance it costs to obtain it; without those, it could not be attained.

A sick woman once bought a cocoon . It held a very beautiful butterfly with magnificent wings. She hoped to see it emerge from the cocoon in her chamber. She watched it eagerly as spring drew on.

Finally, she was delighted to see the butterfly beginning to emerge. But it seemed to have great difficulty. It pushed, and strained, and struggled. It made so little headway that she concluded it must need help. With a pair of delicate scissors, she clipped the tight cord that bound the cocoon's opening.

Immediately the cocoon opened wide, and the butterfly escaped without any further struggle. She congratulated herself on her experiment's success. But, something was wrong with the butterfly.

It was all out of the cocoon, it's true. But, its great wings were lifeless and colorless. They dragged behind it, a useless burden. For a few days it lived a miserable sickly life, and then died, without having once lifted its powerless wings. The lady was sorely disappointed and could not understand it. But when she related the circumstance to a naturalist, he told her that it had all been her own fault. That it took just that pushing and struggling to send the life fluid into the wings' veins. Her misguided kindness in shortening the struggle had left the wings lifeless and colorless.

So, our spiritual wings need the struggle of resisting temptation. To save us from it would weaken our souls' power to "mount up with wings as eagles." It would also deny us the "crown of life" promised to those who endure.
