It is in the knowledge of God's Fatherliness, revealed by the Holy Spirit, that the power of prayer will be found to root and grow. In the infinite tenderness, pity, and patience of the infinite Father, in His loving readiness to hear and to help, the life of prayer has its joy. Oh, let us take time until the Spirit has made these words to us spirit and truth, filling heart and life: 'Our Father in heaven.' Then we are indeed within the veil, in the secret place of power where prayer always prevails. ' Hallowed be your name. ' Matthew 6:9. There is something here that strikes us at once. While we ordinarily first bring our own needs to God in prayer and then think of what belongs to God and His interests, the Master reverses the order. First, Thy name, Thy kingdom, Thy will; then, give us , forgive us , lead us , deliver us . Matthew 6:10- 13. The lesson is of more importance than we think. In true worship, the Father must be first, He must be all. The sooner I learn to forget myself in the desire that He may be glorified, the richer the blessing that prayer will bring to me. No one ever loses what he sacrifices for the Father. This must influence all our prayers. There are two sorts of prayer: personal and intercessory. The latter ordinarily occupies the lesser part of our time and energy. This may not be. Christ has opened the school of prayer specially to train intercessors for the great work of bringing down, by their faith and prayer, the blessings of His work and love in the world. There can be no deep growth in prayer unless this is made our aim. The little child may ask the father only what it needs for itself; and yet it soon learns to say, “Give some for sister too.” But the grown-up son, who only lives for the father's interest and takes charge of the father's business, asks more largely and gets all that is asked. And Jesus would train us to the blessed life of consecration and service, in which our interests are all subordinate to the Name, Kingdom, and the Will of the Father. Let us live for this, and let, on each act of adoration, Our Father! there follow in the same breath, Your Name, Your Kingdom, Your Will;—for this, we look up and long. 'Hallowed be your name...' Matthew 6:9. What name? This new name of Father. The word Holy is the central word of the Old Testament; the name Father of the New. In this name of Love, all the holiness and glory of God are now to be revealed. And how is the name to be hallowed? By God Himself: 'And I will vindicate the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations.' Ezekiel 36:23. Our prayer must be that in ourselves, in all God's children, in the presence of the world, God Himself would reveal the holiness, the Divine power, the hidden glory of the name of Father. The Spirit of the Father is the Holy Spirit: it is only when we yield ourselves to be led by Him , that the name will be hallowed in our prayers and lives. Let us learn the prayer: 'Our Father, hallowed be your name.' 'Your kingdom come.' Matthew 6:10. The Father is a King and has a kingdom. The son and heir of a king has no higher ambition than the glory of his father's kingdom. In times of war or danger, this becomes his passion; he can think of nothing else. The children of the Father are here in the enemy's territory, where the kingdom, which is in heaven, is not yet fully manifested. What is more natural than that, when they learn to hallow the Father's name, they should long and cry with deep enthusiasm: 'Your kingdom come.' Matthew 6:10. The coming of the kingdom is the one great event on which the revelation of the Father's glory, the blessedness of His children, and the salvation of the world depends. In our prayers too, the coming of the kingdom waits. Shall we not join in the deep longing cry of the redeemed: 'Your kingdom come'? Let us learn it in the school of Jesus. 'Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.' Matthew 6:10. This petition is too frequently applied alone to the suffering of the will of God. In heaven, God's will is done , and the Master teaches the child to ask that the will may be done on earth just as in heaven: in the spirit of adoring submission and ready obedience. Because the will of God is the glory of heaven, the doing of it is the blessedness of heaven. As the will is done, the kingdom of heaven comes into the heart. And wherever faith has accepted the Father's love, obedience accepts the Father's will. The surrender to, and the prayer for a life of heaven-like obedience, is the spirit of childlike prayer. 'Give us this day our daily bread.' Matthew 6:11 . When first the child has yielded himself to the Father in the care of His Name, His Kingdom, and His Will, he has full liberty to ask for his daily bread. A master cares for the food of his servant, a general of his soldiers, and the father of his child. And will not the Father in heaven care for the child who has in prayer given himself up to His interests? We may indeed in full confidence say: Father, I live for your honour and your work; I know you care for me. Consecration to God and His will gives wonderful liberty in prayer for temporal things: the whole earthly life is given to the Father's loving care. 'And forgive us our debts as we also have forgiven our debtors.' Matthew 6:12. As bread is the first need of the body, so is forgiveness for the soul. And the provision for the one is as sure as for the other. We are children, but our right of access to the Father's presence we owe to the precious blood and the forgiveness it has won for us. Let us beware of the prayer for forgiveness becoming a formality: only what is really confessed is really forgiven. Let us in faith accept the forgiveness as promised: as a spiritual reality, an actual transaction between God and us, it is the entrance into all the Father's love and all the privileges of children. Such forgiveness, as a living experience, is impossible without a forgiving spirit to others: as forgiven expresses the heavenward, so forgiving the earthward, the relation of God's child. In each prayer, to the Father, I must be able to say that I know of no one whom I do not heartily love. ‘And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil . ’ Matthew 6:13. Our daily bread, the pardon of our sins, and then our being kept from all sin and the power of the evil one, in these three petitions all our personal need is comprehended. The prayer for bread and pardon must be accompanied by the surrender to live in all things in holy obedience to the Father's will, and the believing prayer in everything to be kept by the power of the indwelling Spirit from the power of the evil one. Children of God! it is thus Jesus who would have us pray to the Father in heaven. O let His Name, Kingdom, and Will, have the first place in our love; His providing, pardoning, and keeping love will be our sure portion. So the prayer will lead us up to the true child-life: the Father to the child, the Father for the child. We shall understand how Father and child, the Thine and the Our , are all one, and how the heart that begins its prayer with the God- devoted Thine, will have the power in faith to speak out the Our too. Such prayer will, indeed, be the fellowship and interchange of love, always bringing us back in trust and worship to Him who is not only the Beginning but the End: 'For thy is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever, Amen.' Matthew 6:13. Son of the Father, teach us to pray, 'Our Father.' You who art the only begotten Son, teach us, we beseech you, to pray, 'Our Father.' We thank you, Lord, for these Living Blessed Words which you have given us. We thank you for the millions who in them have learned to know and worship the Father, and for what they have been to us. Lord! it is as if we needed days and weeks in your school with each separate petition; so deep and full are they. But we look to you to lead us deeper into their meaning: do it, we pray to you, for your name's sake; your name is Son of the Father. Lord! You once said: “No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.” Matthew 11:27. And again: 'I made known to them your name, and I will continue to make it known, that the love with which you have loved me may be in them, and I in them.' John 17:26. Lord Jesus! reveal to us the Father. Let His name, His infinite Father-love, the love with which He loved you, according to your prayer, BE IN US. Then shall we say aright, 'Our Father!' Then shall we apprehend your teaching, and the first spontaneous breathing of our heart will be: 'Our Father, Your Name, Your Kingdom, Your Will.' And we shall bring our needs and our sins and our temptations to Him in the confidence that the love of such a Father cares for all. Blessed Lord! We are your scholars. We trust you; teach us to pray, ' Our Father. ' Amen . THE END

fields.title: The Secret of Guidance
fields.body_html:
God's guidance is essential for a Christian's life, work, and peace.

Believers need to align themselves with His will to receive His provision and avoid self-driven failures. Through Biblical examples like Abraham, Moses, and the apostles, we see the importance of seeking divine direction through prayer, studying Scripture, and trusting in God's timing. Believers are reminded to maintain pure motives, surrender personal desires, and wait patiently, as God’s will is often revealed gradually, guiding step by step. Ultimately, obedience and dependence on God assure clarity and fulfillment of His purpose.

Many children of God worry about guidance. I will offer some tips on knowing how our Father wants us to walk and the work He wants us to do. Our power and peace depend on knowing where God wants us to be and being there. We cannot exaggerate their importance.

The manna only falls where the cloudy pillar broods. But, you can certainly find it on the sands that glowed under the heavenly fire's flashing light a few hours ago. They are now shadowed by the fleecy cloud canopy. If we are where our heavenly Father wants us to be, we are sure He will provide food, clothing, and everything else. When He sends His servants to Cherith, He will make even the ravens bring them food.

How much of our Christian work has failed? It is because we have insisted on starting it ourselves. We should have sought to know what God was doing and where He wanted us! We dream bright dreams of success. We try to command it. We call to our aid all kinds of quick fixes, questionable or otherwise. At last we turn back, disheartened and ashamed. We are like children, torn and scratched by thorns, and soiled by the quagmire. None of this would have come about if only we had been, from the first, under God’s perfect guidance. He might test us, but He would not allow us to fail.

The child of God, wanting to know his Father's will, turns to the sacred Book. It restores his faith. It shows how, in all ages, God has guided those who dared to trust Him. But, they must have been as perplexed as we are now. We know how Abraham left his kin and country. With no guide but God, he crossed the trackless desert to a land unknown to him. We know how, for forty years, the Israelites were led through the red sandstone and sand of the Sinai Peninsula.

We know how, in entering the Promised Land, Joshua faced unknown lands and great, warlike nations. He looked to the Captain of the Lord's hosts, who leads to victory. We know that, in the early church, the apostles solved tough problems. They laid down principles to guide the church until the end of time. This was because the Holy Spirit revealed to them what to do and say. The promises for guidance are unmistakable. Psalm 32:8: "I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with my eye upon you." This is God's promise to those whose sins are forgiven. They are more eager to see a hint of His will than horses are to feel the bit.

Proverbs 3:6: “In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make straight your paths.” This is a sure word on which we may rest. But, we must trust with all our heart and not lean on our own understanding. Isaiah 58:11: "And the LORD will guide you continually and satisfy your desire in scorched places and make your bones strong." If He did not always guide us, we could not think He could guide us at all. Life's greatest events hinge on tiny points. Like the huge rocking stones in western England. A pebble may alter the flow of a stream. The growth of a grain of mustard seed may determine the rainfall of a continent. We are bidden to seek guidance for all of life and its essentials.

John 8:12: Again Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world.” Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life." This refers to the wilderness wanderings. The Master promises to be, to all faithful souls in their pilgrimage to the City of God, what the cloudy pillar was to the Israelites on their march to the Promised Land. These are but samples. The Bible's treasure is full of insights. They shine like stars, guiding a lost traveler at sea. The prophet sums up the heritage of the Lord's servants. He says of the Holy City, "All your children shall be taught by the LORD, and great shall be the peace of your children." (Isaiah 54:13).

Some may think, with their timid hearts, that everyone in the Bible was helped. But, they are left without help. They seem to have faced life's mysteries. They long to know what to do. But, no angel has come to tell them. No iron gate has opened in the prison of circumstances.

Some lay the blame on their own stupidity. Their minds are blunt and dull. They cannot catch God’s meaning, which would be clear to others.

Their fear of making mistakes prevents them from understanding what is right. “Who is blind but my servant, or deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is blind as my dedicated one, or blind as the servant of the LORD?” (Isaiah 42:19). Yet, how do we treat our children? One child is so bright that a hint shows the way. Another, born dull, cannot grasp your meaning quickly. Do you only let the clever one know what you want? Will you not take the other upon your knee and make clear to him the confusing directions?

Does not the tiny child's distress, to know he may obey, weave a stronger bond than that which binds you to the rest? Oh, weary, perplexed, and stupid children! Believe in God's great love. Trust it. He will meet your needs and come down to your ignorance. "He will tend his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms; he will carry them in his bosom, and gently lead those that are with young.” (Isaiah 40:11). We must attend to certain practical directions to be led into the mind of the Lord.

Our Motives Must Be Pure “Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light, but when it is bad, your body is full of darkness” (Luke 11:34). You have been much in darkness lately, and this passage will point up the reason. Your eye has been distracted from its primary focus. A spiritual squint has blurred your vision.

It has hindered you from seeing signs of God's will, which would have been as clear as noon. We must be very careful in judging our motives. We should search them, as the Commons' detectives search each stranger who enters. By God's grace, we are free from gross sin. But, we are still prone to the subtle workings of the self in our holiest, loveliest hours. It poisons our motives.

It breathes decay on our fairest fruit-bearing. It whispers seductive flatteries into our pleased ears. It turns the spirit from its holy purpose. The masses of iron on ocean steamers deflect the compass needle from the pole.

If there is any thought of personal gain, we can't know God's purpose for us. The door must remain firmly shut against all these if we are to hear the still small voice. We must exclude all cross-lights. Only then could we see the Urim and Thummim stones. They would brighten with God's "Yes" or darken with His "No." Ask the Holy Spirit for a single eye. Let it inspire in you one aim alone: that which drove our Lord. It let Him cry to the Father, "For we never came with flattery, as you know, nor with a pretext for greed—God is witness." Nor did we seek glory from people, whether from you or others. Though we could have made demands as apostles of Christ." (1 Thessalonians 2:5-6) Then, "If then your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly bright, as when a lamp with its rays gives you light" (Luke 11:36). We must surrender our will.

“I can do nothing on my own. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just because I seek not my own will but the will of him who sent me.” (John 5:30). This was the secret that Jesus practiced and taught.

He repeatedly insisted that a surrendered will was the key to perfect knowledge. “If anyone’s will is to do God’s will, he will know whether the teaching is from God or whether I am speaking on my own authority.” (John 7:17).

An extinguished will differs from a surrendered one. God does not demand that we crush our wills, like a fakir’s unused arms. He only asks that we should say “Yes” to Him. We ought to be as flexible toward Him as the willow branch is to the practised hand.

Many times, as the steamer neared the bank, I watched the little lad. He took his place beneath the poop, eyes and ears fixed on the captain. He waited to shout each word to the grimy engineers below. I often longed for my will to, as the Lord's, obey. I wanted my words to match God's, so all my lower nature might obey.

It is for the lack of this subordination that we so often miss the guidance we seek. There is a secret controversy between our will and God’s. And we will never be right till we have let Him take, break, and make. Oh! Do seek for that. If you cannot give, let Him take. If you are not willing, confess that you are willing to become willing. Hand yourself over to Him to work in you, to will and to do His own good pleasure. We must be like plastic clay. We should be ready to take any shape that the great Potter may choose. Only then can we detect His guidance.

We must Seek Information for Our Mind. This is undoubtedly the next step. God has given us these wonderful faculties of brainpower, and He will not ignore them.

In grace, He does not cancel His marvellous gifts. But, He uses them to communicate His purposes and thoughts. We must, then, feed our minds with facts and reliable information. We should learn from human experience and, above all, the Word of God. It is admirable how full the Bible is of biography and history. Hardly any crisis in our lives can match those wondrous pages. There is no book like the Bible for casting a light on the dark landing of human life.

We don’t need to run to our friends for advice. But, we should gather reliable information. It can feed and strengthen our holy thoughts and purpose. We must decide, as God shall teach us. His voice may come through sanctified common sense, using what we have learned. At times, God may ask us to act against our reason. These times are very rare. Our duty will be so clear that there can be no mistake. But, for the most part, God will speak in the results of a careful weighing of the pros and cons.

An angel rescued Peter from prison. But, after a street or two, the angel left him to consider the matter. That is the way God treats us too. He will dictate a miraculous course by miraculous methods. But when the ordinary light of reason is adequate to the task, He will leave us to act as occasion may serve.

We Must Be Much in Prayer for Guidance The Psalms have many pleas for clear direction: "Teach me your way, O Lord, and lead me on a level path because of my enemies."” (Psalm 27:11). It is the law of our Father’s house that His children must ask for what they want.

"If any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives to all without reproach. And God will give it to him." In a time of change and crisis, we must pray. We should be on our knees, but also in a sweet, inward prayer. It is a spirit that constantly asks God to show His will. We seek to have His will impressed upon our spirit, like heavenly bodies on prepared paper.

The trustful believer, wrapped in prayer, may tread the deck of the ocean steamer night after night. He who points the stars will not fail to guide a soul whose only aim is to do His will.

A good prayer is to ask God to shut doors, close the way, and halt all ventures against His will at their start. From the outset, put the matter in God's hands. He will shatter any project that is not according to His holy will.

We must wait for God's plan to unfold. We should trust His impressions and His word, which His providence supports. We should also wait in silence until these three converge into one point.

Sometimes it looks as if we are bound to act. Everyone says we must act. Things are so desperate that we must. The Egyptians are behind us. Inaccessible cliffs are on our sides. The sea is in front. It is not easy at such times to stand still and see the salvation of God, but we must. Saul made the biggest mistake of his life. He compelled himself and offered a sacrifice, thinking Samuel was late in coming. God may delay to come in the guise of His providence.

There was delay before Sennacherib’s host lay like withered leaves around the Holy City. There was a delay before Jesus walked on the sea at dawn or hastened to raise Lazarus. There was a delay before the angel sped to Peter's side on the night before his expected martyrdom. God waits long enough to test patience of faith, but not a moment behind the extreme hour of need. “For still the vision awaits its appointed time; it hastens to the end—it will not lie. If it seems slow, wait for it; it will surely come; it will not delay. (Habakkuk 2:3).

It is remarkable how God guides us by circumstances. At one moment, the way may seem blocked. Then, a trivial incident occurs. It may not seem much to others. But, to the keen eye of faith, it speaks volumes. Sometimes these signs are repeated in different ways in answer to prayer. They are not random results of chance, but the opening up of circumstances in the direction in which we should walk. And they begin to multiply as we advance toward our goal, just as lights do as we near a populous town when darting through the land by night express.

Sometimes, men sigh for an angel to show them the way. That means the time has not yet come for them to move. If you do not know what you ought to do, stand still until you do. When it's time for action, circumstances will sparkle like glow worms along your path. You will be so sure you are right, when God’s three witnesses agree, that you could not be more sure though an angel beckoned you on.

Our daily life is a reliable sign of God's will. This is true when it aligns with the Spirit's promptings and the Word of God. So long as they are stationary, wait. When you must act, they will open.

A way will be made through oceans, rivers, wastes, and rocks. We often make a great mistake. We think that God is not guiding us, because we cannot see far ahead. But this is not His method. He only undertakes that the steps of a good man should be ordered by the Lord. Not next year, but tomorrow. Not the next mile, but the next yard. Not the whole pattern, but the next stitch in the canvas. If you expect more than this, you will be disappointed and get back into the dark. But, this will secure for you leading in the right way. You will acknowledge this when you review it from the hilltops of glory.

We cannot ponder too deeply the lessons of the cloud. It is given in the exquisite picture-lesson on guidance (Numbers 9:15–23).

" On the day that the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the testimony. And at evening it was over the tabernacle like the appearance of fire until morning. So it was always: the cloud covered it by day and the appearance of fire by night. And whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, after that the people of Israel set out, and in the place where the cloud settled down, there the people of Israel camped. At the command of the LORD the people of Israel set out, and at the command of the LORD they camped. As long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they remained in camp. Even when the cloud continued over the tabernacle many days, the people of Israel kept the charge of the LORD and did not set out ." (Numbers 9:15-19) “ Sometimes the cloud was a few days over the tabernacle, and according to the command of the LORD they remained in camp; then according to the command of the LORD they set out. And sometimes the cloud remained from evening until morning. And when the cloud lifted in the morning, they set out, or if it continued for a day and a night, when the cloud lifted, they set out. Whether it was two days, or a month, or a longer time that the cloud continued over the tabernacle abiding there, the people of Israel remained in camp and did not set out, but when it lifted, they set out. At the command of the LORD, they camped, and at the command of the LORD, they set out. “They kept the charge of the LORD, at the command of the LORD by Moses.”(Numbers 9:20-23) Let us look high enough for guidance. Let us encourage our souls to wait only upon God until He gives it. Let us cultivate that meekness that He will guide in judgment. Let us seek to understand with great urgency, so we may incline ourselves to see the least sign of His will. Let us stand with girded loins and lighted lamps, prompting us to obey. Blessed are those servants. The right way will lead them to the golden city of the saints. I have waited and prayed for months. I am sure of my heavenly Father's guidance. I urge any troubled readers to wait for the Lord. He will show His will in time.

Let it inspire in you one aim alone: that which drove our Lord. It let Him cry to the Father, "For we never came with flattery, as you know, nor with a pretext for greed—God is witness." Nor did we seek glory from people, whether from you or others. Though we could have made demands as apostles of Christ." (1 Thessalonians 2:5-6) Then, "If then your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly bright, as when a lamp with its rays gives you light" (Luke 11:36). We must surrender our will. “I can do nothing on my own. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just because I seek not my own will but the will of him who sent me.” (John 5:30). This was the secret that Jesus practiced and taught. He repeatedly insisted that a surrendered will was the key to perfect knowledge. “If anyone’s will is to do God’s will, he will know whether the teaching is from God or whether I am speaking on my own authority.” (John 7:17). An extinguished will differs from a surrendered one. God does not demand that we crush our wills, like a fakir’s unused arms. He only asks that we should say “Yes” to Him. We ought to be as flexible toward Him as the willow branch is to the practised hand. Many times, as the steamer neared the bank, I watched the little lad. He took his place beneath the poop, eyes and ears fixed on the captain. He waited to shout each word to the grimy engineers below. I often longed for my will to, as the Lord's, obey. I wanted my words to match God's, so all my lower nature might obey. It is for the lack of this subordination that we so often miss the guidance we seek. There is a secret controversy between our will and God’s. And we will never be right till we have let Him take, break, and make. Oh! Do seek for that. If you cannot give, let Him take. If you are not willing, confess that you are willing to become willing. Hand yourself over to Him to work in you, to will and to do His own good pleasure. We must be like plastic clay. We should be ready to take any shape that the great Potter may choose. Only then can we detect His guidance. We must Seek Information for Our Mind. This is undoubtedly the next step. God has given us these wonderful faculties of brainpower, and He will not ignore them. In grace, He does not cancel His marvellous gifts. But, He uses them to communicate His purposes and thoughts. We must, then, feed our minds with facts and reliable information. We should learn from human experience and, above all, the Word of God. It is admirable how full the Bible is of biography and history. Hardly any crisis in our lives can match those wondrous pages. There is no book like the Bible for casting a light on the dark landing of human life. We don’t need to run to our friends for advice. But, we should gather reliable information. It can feed and strengthen our holy thoughts and purpose. We must decide, as God shall teach us. His voice may come through sanctified common sense, using what we have learned. At times, God may ask us to act against our reason. These times are very rare. Our duty will be so clear that there can be no mistake. But, for the most part, God will speak in the results of a careful weighing of the pros and cons. An angel rescued Peter from prison. But, after a street or two, the angel left him to consider the matter. That is the way God treats us too. He will dictate a miraculous course by miraculous methods. But when the ordinary light of reason is adequate to the task, He will leave us to act as occasion may serve. We Must Be Much in Prayer for Guidance The Psalms have many pleas for clear direction: "Teach me your way, O Lord, and lead me on a level path because of my enemies."” (Psalm 27:11). It is the law of our Father’s house that His children must ask for what they want. "If any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives to all without reproach. And God will give it to him." In a time of change and crisis, we must pray. We should be on our knees, but also in a sweet, inward prayer. It is a spirit that constantly asks God to show His will. We seek to have His will impressed upon our spirit, like heavenly bodies on prepared paper. The trustful believer, wrapped in prayer, may tread the deck of the ocean steamer night after night. He who points the stars will not fail to guide a soul whose only aim is to do His will. A good prayer is to ask God to shut doors, close the way, and halt all ventures against His will at their start. From the outset, put the matter in God's hands. He will shatter any project that is not according to His holy will. We must wait for God's plan to unfold. We should trust His impressions and His word, which His providence supports. We should also wait in silence until these three converge into one point. Sometimes it looks as if we are bound to act. Everyone says we must act. Things are so desperate that we must. The Egyptians are behind us. Inaccessible cliffs are on our sides. The sea is in front. It is not easy at such times to stand still and see the salvation of God, but we must. Saul made the biggest mistake of his life. He compelled himself and offered a sacrifice, thinking Samuel was late in coming. God may delay to come in the guise of His providence. There was delay before Sennacherib’s host lay like withered leaves around the Holy City. There was a delay before Jesus walked on the sea at dawn or hastened to raise Lazarus. There was a delay before the angel sped to Peter's side on the night before his expected martyrdom. God waits long enough to test patience of faith, but not a moment behind the extreme hour of need. “For still the vision awaits its appointed time; it hastens to the end—it will not lie. If it seems slow, wait for it; it will surely come; it will not delay. (Habakkuk 2:3). It is remarkable how God guides us by circumstances. At one moment, the way may seem blocked. Then, a trivial incident occurs. It may not seem much to others. But, to the keen eye of faith, it speaks volumes. Sometimes these signs are repeated in different ways in answer to prayer. They are not random results of chance, but the opening up of circumstances in the direction in which we should walk. And they begin to multiply as we advance toward our goal, just as lights do as we near a populous town when darting through the land by night express. Sometimes, men sigh for an angel to show them the way. That means the time has not yet come for them to move. If you do not know what you ought to do, stand still until you do. When it's time for action, circumstances will sparkle like glow worms along your path. You will be so sure you are right, when God’s three witnesses agree, that you could not be more sure though an angel beckoned you on. Our daily life is a reliable sign of God's will. This is true when it aligns with the Spirit's promptings and the Word of God. So long as they are stationary, wait. When you must act, they will open. A way will be made through oceans, rivers, wastes, and rocks. We often make a great mistake. We think that God is not guiding us, because we cannot see far ahead. But this is not His method. He only undertakes that the steps of a good man should be ordered by the Lord. Not next year, but tomorrow. Not the next mile, but the next yard. Not the whole pattern, but the next stitch in the canvas. If you expect more than this, you will be disappointed and get back into the dark. But, this will secure for you leading in the right way. You will acknowledge this when you review it from the hilltops of glory. We cannot ponder too deeply the lessons of the cloud. It is given in the exquisite picture-lesson on guidance (Numbers 9:15–23). " On the day that the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the testimony. And at evening it was over the tabernacle like the appearance of fire until morning. So it was always: the cloud covered it by day and the appearance of fire by night. And whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, after that the people of Israel set out, and in the place where the cloud settled down, there the people of Israel camped. At the command of the LORD the people of Israel set out, and at the command of the LORD they camped. As long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they remained in camp. Even when the cloud continued over the tabernacle many days, the people of Israel kept the charge of the LORD and did not set out ." (Numbers 9:15-19) “ Sometimes the cloud was a few days over the tabernacle, and according to the command of the LORD they remained in camp; then according to the command of the LORD they set out. And sometimes the cloud remained from evening until morning. And when the cloud lifted in the morning, they set out, or if it continued for a day and a night, when the cloud lifted, they set out. Whether it was two days, or a month, or a longer time that the cloud continued over the tabernacle abiding there, the people of Israel remained in camp and did not set out, but when it lifted, they set out. At the command of the LORD, they camped, and at the command of the LORD, they set out. “They kept the charge of the LORD, at the command of the LORD by Moses.”(Numbers 9:20-23) Let us look high enough for guidance. Let us encourage our souls to wait only upon God until He gives it. Let us cultivate that meekness that He will guide in judgment. Let us seek to understand with great urgency, so we may incline ourselves to see the least sign of His will. Let us stand with girded loins and lighted lamps, prompting us to obey. Blessed are those servants. The right way will lead them to the golden city of the saints. I have waited and prayed for months. I am sure of my heavenly Father's guidance. I urge any troubled readers to wait for the Lord. He will show His will in time.

fields.title: Where Am I Wrong?
fields.body_html:
The Christian soul yearns for joy, peace, and a closer walk with God, but this comes from recognizing that true contentment and light come from alignment with God’s will, not through mere emotions. It is best to acknowledge that while some naturally feel joyful, others carry a sad spirit, yet both can find peace in surrendering their will to God. This chapter explores how disobedience, unchecked sins, or excessive self-focus create barriers to experiencing God’s blessings. Through consistent communion with God, obedience, and reliance on Christ rather than feelings, believers are encouraged to find rest in God’s unchanging love.

This is your eager question, O Christian soul, and your bitter complaint. You see a light, a joy, a power in people you know. You envy it, which oppresses you. But, you should thank God for it. It's good to be dissatisfied with our low aspirations. It can lead us to seek a sweeter, nobler, and more triumphant life. The restless sleeper is near awakening. The morning light now shines around the bed, where he has slept too long. For, anything that becomes visible is light. Therefore it says, “Awake, O sleeper, and arise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.” (Ephesians 5:14).

We must, yet, remember that personalities differ. Some seem born in the dark, and carry a tendency to sadness with them through life. Their nature is set to a minor key and responds with ease to depression.

They always look on the dark side of things and in the bluest of skies discover the cloud no bigger than a man’s hand. Theirs is a dark path. Tiny sunbeams struggle to break through the thick, leafy canopy above. You may have such a temperament. If so, don't expect the same joy that others feel. And, don't complain if you don't feel it.

Your Savior’s hands made this burden for you. You must carry it for Him. Do not complain, show it to others, or let it master your spirit. Bear it silently, and glorify God through it all. But it may be impossible to win the joy of others. At least, there may be rest, victory, and peace. They are heaven's best gifts to man.

We must also remember that emotion is no true test of our spiritual state. A right heart often shows in a glad heart. So, good health usually shows in high spirits. But it is not always so. In other words, the absence of joy does not always prove that the heart is wrong. It may do so, but it will not always happen. The wilderness may have overtaxed Elijah's nervous system. After the long strain of Carmel and his flight, he lay on the sand and asked to die. God met that request, not with a rebuke, but with food and sleep.

The Lord has darkened your land. He wants to test if you love Him for Himself or for His gifts.

Perhaps, life has reached a Gethsemane. A Father's hand places a bitter cup to our lips, though only a Judas appears. We feel anguish in our struggle to renounce our will. It is only possible to lie upon the ground, with strong crying and tears, which the night wind bears to God. Under such circumstances as these, exuberant joy is out of place.

Sombre colours become the tried and suffering soul.

High spirits would be as unbecoming here as cheerfulness in the home shadowed by death. At such times, we should manifest patience, courage, and faith as the suitable graces. Yet, with all that, many of us are at fault. We are missing a blessedness that would make us radiant with the light of paradise. This loss is due to some flaw in our character. We should find and fix it.

You Do Not Distinguish Between Your Standing and Your Experience Our experiences are as fickle as April weather. Now sunshine, now cloud. Lights and shadows chase each other over miles of wild fields or a foamy sea. But our standing in Jesus changes not. It is like Himself—the same yesterday, today, and forever. It did not come from us. It came from His everlasting love. It, foreseeing all we would be, loved us despite it all. We have not purchased it, but His precious blood. It pleads for us with great strength and effectiveness when our faith is weak. It is not maintained by us, but by the Holy Spirit.

If we have fled to Jesus for salvation, we are one with Him forever. We have sheltered under Him, relying on and trusting Him, though with some doubts. We were one with Him in the grave; one with Him on Easter morning; one with Him when He sat down at God’s right hand. We are one with Him now. He stands in the light of His Father's smile. It's like a swimmer's limbs are one with his head. The sun's warm glory encircles the head alone. The waves hide the arms and legs. No doubt or depression can affect our acceptance with God through the blood of Jesus. That is an eternal fact.

You may not realize this. But, have your moods affected your standing in Jesus? A wealthy heiress's fortune could change with her spending money. Our standing in Jesus is our invested capital. Our emotions, at best, are like our spending money. It is always passing through our pocket or purse, never the same. Consider how you feel. Build on the rock of what Jesus is, has done, is doing, and will do for you, forever.

You Live Too Much in Your Feelings, Too Little in Your Will. We have no direct control over our feelings, but we have over our will. Our wills are ours, to make them God’s. God does not hold us responsible for what we feel, but for what we will. In His sight, we are not what we feel, but what we will. Let us not live in the summerhouse of emotion. Instead, let us live in the stronghold of the will, devoted to God's will.

At the Lord's Table, holy emotion often fills the soul. The tides rise high. Joy's powerful waves knock loudly against the floodgates. Every part of nature joins in a choral hymn of praise. But the next day comes. Life must be faced in the grimy counting house, the dingy shop, the noisy factory, and the godless workroom. The soul, comparing yesterday's joy with today's struggle, doubts its devotion to the Lord.

But, at such a time, how fair it is to remark that the will has not altered its position by a hair's breadth. And to look up and say: "My God, the spring tide of emotion has passed away like a summer brook. But in my heart, you know I am devoted and loyal.

I long to be only for You, as in that blessed moment at Your feet." This is an offering with which God is well pleased. And thus we may live a calm and peaceful life.

You Have Disobeyed Some Clear Command. A soul sometimes comes to its spiritual adviser, saying: "I have no joy, and little for years." “Did you once have it?”

“Yes, for some time after my conversion to God.”

"Are you aware that you disobeyed a specific command?

"It came into your life, but you shrank from it."

The face fell. Tears filled the eyes. The answer came, with difficulty: "Yes, years ago, I thought God required something of me. But I felt I could not do what He wished."

I was uneasy for some time about it, but after a while it seemed to fade from my mind, and now it does rarely trouble me.” "Ah, soul, that's where you went wrong. You will never get right until you go back through the weary years to where you dropped the thread of obedience. You must perform that one thing God demanded of you long ago. It is why you left the narrow path of blind obedience. Is this not the cause of depression for thousands of Christians? They are God’s children, but they are disobedient children.

The Bible rings with one long demand for obedience. The key phrase of the book of Deuteronomy is, “Observe and Do.”

The burden of Christ’s farewell discourse is, “If you love me, you will keep my commandments.” We must not question or reply, or excuse ourselves. We must not pick and choose our way. We must not take some commands and reject others. We must not believe that obedience elsewhere will make up for disobedience in one area. God gives one command at a time, borne in upon us, not in one way only, but in many; by this He tests us. If we obey in this, He will flood our souls with blessings and lead us forward into new paths and pastures. But if we refuse, we will remain stagnant and waterlogged. We will make no progress in our Christian experience and lack both power and joy.

You Are Permitting Some Known Evil When water stands, the particles of silt betray themselves as they fall one by one to the bottom. So if you are quiet, you may become aware of the presence in your soul of permitted evil. Dare to consider it. Do not avoid the sight like a bankrupt man avoids his ledgers, or a sick man avoids a stethoscope. Consider, in silence, any evil the Spirit of God finds in your soul. It may have lurked in the closets and cloisters of your being for years, suspected but unjudged. But whatever it is, and its history, it brings your daily sorrow.

Does your will you refuse to give up a practice or habit that is foreign to the will of God? Do you permit some secret sin to have its unhindered way in the house of your life? Do your affections roam unrestrained after forbidden objects? Do you cherish any resentment or hatred toward someone with whom you refuse to reconcile? Is there an injustice you won't forgive? A debt you won't pay? A wrong you won't confess?

Are you allowing in yourself something you would condemn in others? You justify it for certain reasons to silence your conscience.

Sometimes, the hindrance of bliss lies not in sins but in burdens that weigh on the soul. Sin is that which is always and everywhere wrong. A weight is anything that hinders the Christian life, but is not a sin. Thus, a thing may be a weight to one that is not so to another. Each must reach complete conviction in his own mind. If the soul knows that anything hinders its life, it must be cast aside. This is true, regardless of the harmlessness or innocent permission of that thing. You must discard it, like the garments of athletes who compete for a prize in wrestling or racing.

You Look Too Much Inward on Self, Instead of Outward on the Lord Jesus The healthiest people don't think about their health. The weak cause disease by overthinking. If you begin to count your heartbeats, you will disturb the rhythmic action of the heart. If you repeatedly imagine a pain anywhere, you will produce it. Some true children of God induce their own darkness by morbid self-scrutiny. They always go back on themselves. They analyze their motives. They rethink past acts of devotion. They compare themselves to themselves. In one form or another, the self is the pivot of their life, even if it is a religious life. What but darkness can result from such a course? At times in our lives, we must look within and check ourselves to avoid others judging us.

But this is only done so that we may turn with the fuller purpose of heart to the Lord. Once you complete it, you don’t need to repeat it.

“Leaving the things behind” is the only safe motto. The question is not if we did our best, but if we did as well as we could at the time. We must not waste our lives cleaning our windows, or in worrying if they are clean. We must enjoy God's blessed light. That light will soon show us what must be cleansed.

It will let us cleanse it with perfect accuracy. Our Lord Jesus is a perfect reservoir of everything the soul of man requires for a blessed and holy life.

To be healthy in soul, we must make much of Him. We must abide in Him, draw from Him, and receive each moment from His fullness. To care for self-more than for Him is like this: Spending much time on the body's senses, but never using them to sense the world outside.

Look unto Jesus. “Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart” (Psalm 37:4). “For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him.” (Psalm 62:5).

You Spend Too Little Time in Communion with God through His Word Long prayers are not necessary. But it is essential to be alone with God. Wait at His door, hear His voice, and linger in Scripture for the Lord's coming at dawn or in the cool of the day. No meetings, no Christian friends, and no activity can replace the neglect of the still hour.

When you feel least inclined for it, there is most need to go into your closet with the door shut. Do for duty’s sake what you cannot do as a pleasure, and you will find it becomes delightful.

You can thrive without food. But you cannot find joy or strength in a Christian life without fellowship with God. When you cannot pray for yourself, begin to pray for others. When your desires fade, take the Bible. Turn each text into a petition. Or, recall your mercies. Then, translate each into praise.

When the Bible bores you, check your appetite. Have you spoiled it with sweets? If so, renounce them. The Word is the wire along which God's voice will come to you. But your heart must be still and your mind focused. “Let me hear what God the Lord will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, to his saints; but let them not turn back to folly.” (Psalm 85:8). More Christians than we can count are suffering from a lack of prayer and Bible study. No one desires a revival more than that of systematic private Bible study. No short and easy method of godliness can dispense with this.

You have never fully surrendered yourself to the authority of the Lord Jesus .

We are His by many ties and rights, but too few of us recognize His lordship. We are willing enough to take Him as Savior but hesitate to make Him King. We forget that God has exalted Him to be Prince, as well as Savior, and the divine order is irreversible.

Those who ignore the Lordship of Jesus cannot build a strong or happy life. Put the sun in its central throne, and all the motions of the planets assume a beautiful order. Put Jesus on the throne of your life, and all things fall into harmony and peace. Seek first the kingdom of God, and all things are yours.

Consecration is the indispensable condition of blessedness. So will light break on your path, such as has not shone there for many days. Yes, "Your sun shall no more go down, nor your moon withdraw. For the Lord will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning shall end.” (Isaiah 60:20).

Do your affections roam unrestrained after forbidden objects? Do you cherish any resentment or hatred toward someone with whom you refuse to reconcile? Is there an injustice you won't forgive? A debt you won't pay? A wrong you won't confess? Are you allowing in yourself something you would condemn in others? You justify it for certain reasons to silence your conscience. Sometimes, the hindrance of bliss lies not in sins but in burdens that weigh on the soul. Sin is that which is always and everywhere wrong. A weight is anything that hinders the Christian life, but is not a sin. Thus, a thing may be a weight to one that is not so to another. Each must reach complete conviction in his own mind. If the soul knows that anything hinders its life, it must be cast aside. This is true, regardless of the harmlessness or innocent permission of that thing. You must discard it, like the garments of athletes who compete for a prize in wrestling or racing. You Look Too Much Inward on Self, Instead of Outward on the Lord Jesus The healthiest people don't think about their health. The weak cause disease by overthinking. If you begin to count your heartbeats, you will disturb the rhythmic action of the heart. If you repeatedly imagine a pain anywhere, you will produce it. Some true children of God induce their own darkness by morbid self-scrutiny. They always go back on themselves. They analyze their motives. They rethink past acts of devotion. They compare themselves to themselves. In one form or another, the self is the pivot of their life, even if it is a religious life. What but darkness can result from such a course? At times in our lives, we must look within and check ourselves to avoid others judging us. But this is only done so that we may turn with the fuller purpose of heart to the Lord. Once you complete it, you don’t need to repeat it. “Leaving the things behind” is the only safe motto. The question is not if we did our best, but if we did as well as we could at the time. We must not waste our lives cleaning our windows, or in worrying if they are clean. We must enjoy God's blessed light. That light will soon show us what must be cleansed. It will let us cleanse it with perfect accuracy. Our Lord Jesus is a perfect reservoir of everything the soul of man requires for a blessed and holy life. To be healthy in soul, we must make much of Him. We must abide in Him, draw from Him, and receive each moment from His fullness. To care for self-more than for Him is like this: Spending much time on the body's senses, but never using them to sense the world outside. Look unto Jesus. “Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart” (Psalm 37:4). “For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him.” (Psalm 62:5). You Spend Too Little Time in Communion with God through His Word Long prayers are not necessary. But it is essential to be alone with God. Wait at His door, hear His voice, and linger in Scripture for the Lord's coming at dawn or in the cool of the day. No meetings, no Christian friends, and no activity can replace the neglect of the still hour. When you feel least inclined for it, there is most need to go into your closet with the door shut. Do for duty’s sake what you cannot do as a pleasure, and you will find it becomes delightful. You can thrive without food. But you cannot find joy or strength in a Christian life without fellowship with God. When you cannot pray for yourself, begin to pray for others. When your desires fade, take the Bible. Turn each text into a petition. Or, recall your mercies. Then, translate each into praise. When the Bible bores you, check your appetite. Have you spoiled it with sweets? If so, renounce them. The Word is the wire along which God's voice will come to you. But your heart must be still and your mind focused. “Let me hear what God the Lord will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, to his saints; but let them not turn back to folly.” (Psalm 85:8). More Christians than we can count are suffering from a lack of prayer and Bible study. No one desires a revival more than that of systematic private Bible study. No short and easy method of godliness can dispense with this. You have never fully surrendered yourself to the authority of the Lord Jesus . We are His by many ties and rights, but too few of us recognize His lordship. We are willing enough to take Him as Savior but hesitate to make Him King. We forget that God has exalted Him to be Prince, as well as Savior, and the divine order is irreversible. Those who ignore the Lordship of Jesus cannot build a strong or happy life. Put the sun in its central throne, and all the motions of the planets assume a beautiful order. Put Jesus on the throne of your life, and all things fall into harmony and peace. Seek first the kingdom of God, and all things are yours. Consecration is the indispensable condition of blessedness. So will light break on your path, such as has not shone there for many days. Yes, "Your sun shall no more go down, nor your moon withdraw. For the Lord will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning shall end.” (Isaiah 60:20).

fields.title: The Secret of Christ’s indwelling
fields.body_html:
Embracing Christ’s presence within provides believers with patience, grace, and spiritual strength, enabling them to live holy lives even amid challenges. By trusting in this inner presence, Christians gain peace and godly power in their daily experiences.

It is fitting that the largest church in the greatest Gentile city is dedicated to the apostle Paul. Gentiles owe him a great debt as the Apostle of the Gentiles. We owe, under the Spirit of God, to him. He unveiled two great mysteries that especially touch us as Gentiles. We cannot discuss, now, the first of these, glorious as it is. It sparked a revolution when first preached by the apostle, despite fierce opposition. Until then, Gentiles had to become Jews before they could be Christians.

They had to go through the synagogue to reach the church. But Paul showed that this was not needful. He proved that Gentiles were equal to Jews in their gospel privileges. They were fellow heirs, and members of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel (Ephesians 3:6). “The mystery is that the Gentiles are fellow heirs. They are members of the same body and partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel.”

The second one deserves more thought. If God's children realized it, they would live divinely. This would silence the enemy and, to some extent, repeat Jesus's life on earth.

The mystery is that the Lord Jesus is willing to dwell within the Gentile heart. Many viewed the expectation for Him to dwell in Abraham's children's hearts as patronizing. But, it was unbelievable to think He could find a home in a Gentile's heart.

This mistake, however, vanished before the truth. He realized that he was unfit to be called an apostle because he had persecuted God's church. God revealed through him, "To them, God chose to reveal among the Gentiles the riches of the glory of this mystery, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory."(Colossians 1:27).

“Master, where do you dwell?” they asked. In reply, Jesus led them from the crowded Jordan bank to a "tent of woven willows," where He stayed for a short time. But if we ask Him now, He will not point to the high, lofty dome of heaven or the splendid stone or marble structure. He will point to the happy spirit that loves, trusts, and obeys Him. “Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and eat with him, and he with me." Revelations 3:20. "Jesus answered him, 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him.” John 14:23. He promised to be within each believer, like a tenant in a house, sap in a branch, and lifeblood in a body.

The Mystery Christ is in the believer. He indwells in the heart by faith. It is like the sun indwelling the lowly flowers that open their petals to its rays. Not because we are good, or because we are making a sincere effort to consecrate ourselves. Not because we keep Him by the tenacity of our love.

But because we believe, and in believing have thrown open all the doors and windows of nature. And He has come in. He entered without making a sound, and we failed to detect His entrance. There was no footfall along the passage.

The golden bells at the bottom of His priestly robe did not betray Him. He arrived at dawn, like nature waking from her winter's sleep and putting on her Creator's robes. But this is the way of Christ. He neither strives nor cries, nor causes His voice to be heard. His tread is so light that it does not break bruised reeds. His breath is so soft that it can re- illuminate dying sparks. So, do not be surprised if you cannot tell the day or the hour when the Son of Man comes to dwell within you. Only believe that He has come. “Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Or do you not realize this about yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless indeed you fail to meet the test!” (2 Corinthians 13:5).

It is very wonderful. The heavens, even the heavens of heavens, with all their light and glory, alone seem worthy of Him. But even there He is not more at home than He is with the humble and contrite spirit that simply trusts in Him.

In His early life, He said the Father dwelt in Him so truly that His words and works were not His, but His Father's. He wants to be in us as His Father was in Him. Our lives should be channels for His hidden self to reach men.

It is not generally recognized. That does not disprove it. We fail to recognize many things in ourselves and in nature around us that are still true. But many whose natures are Christ's temple ignore the wonderful Tenant within. There is a reason for this. He dwells so deep. Below the body's life, which is like a tent's curtain; below the soul's, where thought, feeling, and imagination roam like white-stoled priests in a holy place; below the play of light and shade, will and memory, and the ebb and flow of self-consciousness. There, through the Holy Spirit, Christ dwells. The Shekinah once did in the Most Holy Place, hidden from man's view.

We rarely explore these deeper departments of our being. We are content to live the superficial life of sense. We eat, we drink, and we sleep. We give ourselves to enjoy the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life. We fulfill the desires of the flesh and the mind. Or we abandon ourselves to the pursuit of knowledge and culture, of science and art.

We make short incursions into the realm of morals, that sense of right and wrong that is part of the makeup of men. But, we know too little of the spirit's deeper, mysterious chamber. So, most believers are unaware of their divine, wonderful Resident. He makes the regenerated spirit His home.

One must accept it by faith. We repeat here our constant mistake about the things of God. We try to feel them.

If we feel them, then we believe; otherwise, we take no account of them. We reverse the divine order. We say feeling, FAITH, and FACT. God says FACT, FAITH, and feeling. With Him, feelings matter little. He asks us to accept His Word and to cling to it because He has spoken it. He disregards our feelings.

Scripture tells me that Christ occupies the throne in His ascended glory. He is also within me by the Holy Spirit. I confess I do not feel Him there. Often, amidst the storm of my emotions, I cannot find Him. I cannot hear Him say, "It is I." But, I dare to believe He is there. He is not without me, but within. He is not a transient visitor for a night, but a permanent resident. He is not changed by my shifts in mood, from love to despair. He is always and unchangeably the same.

And I say again and again, “Jesus, You are here. I am not worthy that you should abide under my roof; but you have come. Assert Yourself.

Put down all rule, authority, and power. Come out of your secret chamber, and possess all that is within me, that it may bless your holy name.

Catherine of Siena once spent three days alone, praying for a greater joy in God's presence. Instead, it seemed wicked spirits assailed her with evil thoughts. At length, a great light appeared to descend from above. The devils fled, and the Lord Jesus conversed with her.

Catherine asked Him; “Lord, where were you when my heart was so tormented?”

“I was in your heart,” He answered.

"O Lord, you are everlasting truth," she replied. "I bow before your word. But how can I believe you filled my heart with such detestable thoughts? “Did these thoughts give you pleasure or pain?” He asked.

“An exceeding pain and sadness,” was her reply.

The Lord said, “You were in woe and sadness because I was in the midst of your heart. My presence was what rendered those thoughts unsupportable to you. When the period I had determined for the duration of the combat had elapsed, I sent forth the beams of My light, and the shades of hell were dispelled, because they cannot resist that light.

The Glory of This Mystery When God’s secrets break open, they do so in glory. The wealth of the root hidden in the ground is revealed in the hues of orchids or the scent of roses. The hidden beauty of a beam of light is unravelled in the sevenfold colour of the rainbow.

The swarming, tiny life of southern seas breaks into waves of phosphorescence when cleft by the ship's keel. And whenever the unseen world has revealed itself to mortal eyes, it has been in glory.

It was especially so at the Transfiguration when the Lord’s nature broke from the strong restraint within which He had confined it and revealed itself to man's eye. “And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as light.” (Matthew 17:2).

So when we accept the fact of His existence deeper within us than our own and make it one of the aims of our life to draw on it and develop it, we shall be conscious of a glory transfiguring our life and irradiating ordinary things, which will make earth, with its commonest engagements, like the vestibule of heaven.

Jonathan Edwards’ wife had been the subject of great fluctuations in religious experience and frequent depression till she came to the point of renouncing the world and yielding herself up to be possessed by these mighty truths. In this case, a marvellous change took place. She began to experience a constant, uninterrupted rest; sweet peace and serenity of soul; continual rejoicing in all the works of God’s hands, whether of nature or daily providence; wonderful access to God by prayer, as it was seeing Him and immediately conversing with Him; all tears wiped away; all former troubles and sorrows of life forgotten, except grief for past sins and the dishonour done to Christ in the world; a daily sensible doing and suffering everything for God and doing all with a continual uninterrupted cheerfulness, peace, and Joy.

Such glory—the certain pledge of the glory to be revealed—is within reach of each reader of these lines who will dare day by day to reckon that Christ lives within and will be content to die to the energies and prompting for the self-life so that there may be room for the Christ- life to reveal itself.

“I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.” (Galatians 2:20).

The Riches of the Glory of This Mystery. When this mystery or secret of the divine life in man is apprehended and made use of, it gives great wealth to life. If all the treasures of wisdom, knowledge, power, and grace reside in Jesus, and He has become the cherished and honoured resident of our nature, it is clear that we also must be greatly enriched. It is like a poor man having a millionaire friend come to live with him.

There is a richness of patience. Life is not easy for any of us. No branch escapes the pruning knife; no jewel from the wheel; no child from the rod. People tyrannise and vex us almost beyond endurance. Circumstances strain us till the chords of our hearts threaten to snap. Our nervous system is overtaxed by the rush and competition of our times. Indeed, we need patience.

Never relax the self-watch. Never indulge in unkind or thoughtless criticism of others. Never utter the hasty word or permit the sharp retort. Never complain except to God. Never permit hard and distrustful thoughts to lodge within the soul.

Always be more thoughtful of others than self, to detect the one blue spot in the clouded sky, to be on the alert to find an excuse for those who are forward and awkward; to suffer the aches and pains, the privations and trials of life, sweetly, submissively, trustfully; To drink the bitter cup, with the eye fixed on the Father’s face, without a murmur or complaint: this needs patience, which mere stoicism could never give.

We cannot live such a life till we have learned to avail ourselves of the riches of the indwelling Christ. The beloved apostle speaks of being a partaker of the patience in Jesus. “I, John, your brother and partner in the tribulation and the kingdom and the patient endurance that are in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus. (Revelation 1:9). So may we be that calm, unmurmuring, unreviling patience, which made the Lamb of God dumb before His shearers, is ours.

Robert Hall was once overheard saying amid the heat of an argument, “Calm me, O Lamb of God!” But we may go and say, “Lord Jesus, let Your patience arise in me, as a spring of fresh water in a salty sea.” There are riches of grace. Alone among the great cities of the world, Jerusalem had no river. But the glorious Lord was in the midst of her. He became a place of broad rivers and streams, supplying from Himself. All that rivers gave to cities at the foot of whose walls the welcome water lapped.

This is a picture of what we have, who dare to reckon on the indwelling of our glorious Lord, as King, Lawgiver, and Savior. He makes all grace abound toward us so that we have sufficiency for all emergencies and can abound in every good work. In His strength, ever-rising within us, we can do as much as those endowed with the greatest mental and natural gifts, and we escape the temptations to vainglory and pride by which they are beset.

The grace of purity and self-control, of fervent prayer and understanding in the Scriptures, of love for men and zeal for God, of lowliness and meekness, of gentleness and goodness—all is in Christ; and if Christ is in us, all is ours. Oh, that we would dare to believe it, and draw on it, letting down the pcher of faith into the deep well of Christ’s indwelling, opened within us by the Holy Spirit! It is impossible, in these brief limits, to elaborate further on this wonderful thought. But if only we would meet every call, difficulty, and trial, not saying, as we so often do, “I shall never be able to go through it,” but saying, “I cannot; but Christ is in me, and He can,” we should find that all trials were intended to reveal and unfold the wealth hidden within us, until Christ was formed within us and His life manifested in our mortal bodies (Colossians 1:27).

How do we become more conscious of His life within us? 1. Be still each day for a short time, sitting before God in meditation.

Ask the Holy Spirit to reveal the truth of Christ’s indwelling. Ask God to be pleased to make known what the riches of the glory of this mystery are (Colossians 1:27).

Revere your nature as the temple of the indwelling Lord. As the Easterner bares his feet, and the Westerner his head, on entering the limit of a temple, so be very careful of anything that would defile the body or soil the soul. No beasts must be herded in the temple courts.

Get Christ to drive them out. “Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you? If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him. For God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.” (1 Corinthians 3:16–17).

2. Hate your own life. “If anyone…does not hate… even his own life,” said our Lord, “he cannot be My disciple” (Luke 14:26). And the word translated “life” is soul, the seat and centre of the self-life with its restless energies and activities, its choices and decisions, its ceaseless strivings at independence and leadership. This is the greatest hindrance to our enjoyment of the indwelling Christ. If acquire the habit of saying no, not only to our bad but to our good selves.If we daily deliver ourselves up to death for Jesus’ sake; if we take up our cross and follow the Master, though it be to His grave, we shall become increasingly conscious of being possessed by a richer, deeper, and more divine life than our own.
